It also comprises legs (35) that can be folded up next to the base element (14); support arms (40) with a pivotal connection (42) so each support arm (40) can be moved between a closed position adjacent to the back wall (12), and a second position projecting upward from the back wall (12). Swinging the front panel (20) and the top panel (22) in this way opens the box, and displays the exposed surfaces of the front panel (20) and of the top panel (22). The portable stand enables the display of information on the exposed surfaces, and the display of items within the display chambers (66), for example for the purpose of safety.

outputs.L2:
A portable stand (10) includes a rear wall (12), a base member (14), and a pair of opposing end plates (16). The rear wall and base member extend between the end plates, forming an open-topped, box-shaped container. The stand also includes legs (35) that are foldable into a position alongside the base member (14), as well as support arms (40) mounted by pivot connections (42). Each support arm (40) is movable from a stowed position beside the rear wall (12) to an extended position projecting upwardly from it.

The stand further has a front panel (20) connected by a hinge to the base member (14), allowing the front panel (20) to pivot between a first position in which it serves as the front wall of the box-shaped container and a second position in which it hangs or extends beneath the base member (14). A top panel (22) is hinged to the rear wall (12), enabling it to move between a first position in which it acts as a cover for the container and a second position in which it extends upward above the rear wall (12).

When the front panel (20) and top panel (22) are pivoted into these extended positions, the box is opened and the outer surfaces of both panels are presented for viewing. The container may include several display compartments (66), which are also exposed in this opened configuration. The portable stand can therefore be used to present information on the visible panel surfaces and to exhibit articles placed in the display compartments (66), such as for safety-related purposes.
outputs.L3:
The portable stand is constructed as an open-top, box-like container that includes a back wall, a base element, and two opposed end plates. Together, these components define a stable enclosure suitable for storing, transporting, or supporting display materials.

The stand is also provided with foldable legs and pivoting support arms. These components are movable between a closed position, in which they are compactly arranged for storage or transport, and an upright position, in which they support the stand for use. This allows the stand to be easily carried and then quickly set up at a desired location.

A hinged front panel is connected to the container and is movable between two functional positions. In one position, the front panel acts as the front wall of the container, helping to enclose the stand during transport or storage. In another position, the front panel swings downward to a location below the base element, thereby opening the front of the container and providing additional display area or access to the interior.

The stand further includes a hinged top panel. The top panel may function as a lid when positioned over the open top of the container, protecting the contents inside. Alternatively, the top panel may swing upward to a position above the back wall, where it can serve as an elevated display surface.

When the front panel is swung downward and the top panel is swung upward, the stand is transformed from a compact container into an open display unit. This arrangement exposes display surfaces and may also reveal internal display chambers within the container. These surfaces and chambers can be used to present information, literature, products, or other items, including safety-related materials, in an organized and visible manner.
outputs.L4:
A portable display stand is constructed as an open-top, box-like container that can be easily transported, set up, and used to present information or objects in a clear and organized manner. The stand includes a main container body having internal display chambers or compartments for holding display materials, samples, instructional items, safety equipment, or other objects intended to be viewed. Because the container is open at the top, the interior display area can be accessed conveniently during setup, use, and storage.

The stand is supported by foldable legs that can be extended when the unit is in use and folded away when the unit is being transported or stored. This allows the display stand to be both stable during presentation and compact when not in use. Movable support arms are provided to help hold portions of the stand in an open or display position. These support arms may be adjusted or positioned as needed to support panels, maintain the proper viewing angle, or provide additional stability.

The front and top portions of the container include hinged panels that can be opened outward or upward to create additional display surfaces. When closed, these panels help protect the contents of the stand and allow the unit to function as a portable carrying case. When opened, the panels expose the internal display chambers and may also serve as surfaces for mounting signs, labels, charts, photographs, instructions, warnings, or other informational material. In this way, the stand can quickly be transformed from a compact transportable container into a functional display unit.

This configuration makes the stand especially useful in situations where information must be presented clearly and temporarily at different locations. For example, it may be used for safety displays, training demonstrations, emergency preparedness exhibits, workplace instruction, product presentations, educational demonstrations, or public information displays. The internal chambers can hold relevant items, while the hinged panels and display surfaces can present written or visual information associated with those items.

Overall, the portable stand combines storage, transport, and display functions in a single unit. Its foldable legs allow for convenient setup and breakdown, the movable support arms help maintain the display arrangement, and the hinged panels provide expanded viewing surfaces. As a result, the stand offers a practical and portable solution for presenting information and objects in a neat, accessible, and professional manner.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing a portable safety display stand with foldable legs, hinged front and top panels, support arms, and internal display chambers.
counterfactuals.output: A portable safety display stand includes a collapsible frame having a plurality of foldable legs movable between a deployed support position and a folded transport position. A front panel is hingedly coupled to the frame and is movable between a closed position and an open display position, and a top panel is hingedly coupled to an upper portion of the frame for selectively enclosing or exposing an interior portion of the stand. One or more support arms are connected between the frame and at least one of the hinged panels to retain the panel in the open display position and to provide structural stability during use. The stand further includes one or more internal display chambers configured to receive and present safety equipment, instructional materials, warning indicia, illumination devices, or other emergency-response items. The foldable legs, hinged panels, and support arms cooperate to permit rapid deployment, stable presentation, and compact storage or transport of the safety display stand.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention from a patent claim about a portable stand having a back wall, base, end plates, hinged front panel, hinged lid/top panel, fold-up legs, and display compartments.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a portable, foldable display stand or case designed to be easily transported and then opened into a self-supporting display unit.

It includes a back wall, a base, and end plates that form the main body of the stand. A front panel is hinged to the base and can swing between a closed transport position and an open display position. A top or lid panel is hinged to the back wall and can also open and close. Fold-up legs are attached so the unit can be raised and supported when in use, but folded away for carrying or storage.

Inside or along the stand are display compartments for holding and presenting items, such as merchandise, samples, literature, or promotional materials. When closed, the panels protect the contents and make the unit compact for transport. When opened, the panels and legs convert the case into a stable display stand with accessible compartments.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following patent concept into a clear invention summary: a box-like portable stand with hinged front and top panels that swing open, foldable legs, pivoting support arms, and compartments for displaying safety information and items.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a portable display stand designed to store, transport, and present safety-related information and materials. The stand has a box-like body that can be closed for carrying and opened for use. A front panel and a top panel are hinged to the body and can swing outward to create an expanded display area. Foldable legs support the stand when deployed, allowing it to be set up on the ground or another surface.

Pivoting support arms hold the opened panels in position, providing stability and maintaining the desired display angle. The interior of the stand includes compartments, holders, or storage spaces for displaying safety instructions, warning notices, brochures, equipment, or other related items. When not in use, the panels, legs, and support arms fold back into or against the body, forming a compact portable unit for storage and transport.

Overall, the invention provides a convenient, self-contained, and portable safety information display system that can be quickly set up at job sites, public areas, events, or emergency locations.
